mainTopic: How the rules of private altars (במות) changed over time: the meaning of "rest" and "inheritance," when there is כרת for offering outside, and which services belong only at the big public altar.
overview: The גמרא finishes discussing whether "rest" and "inheritance" in the פסוק mean שילה, ירושלים, or one of each. It also discusses how this affects whether private altars (במות) were allowed in the time of שילה, using מנוח's offering on a rock. Next, רב כהנא says the משנה's rule of no כרת covers only slaughtering outside, not offering up outside. רבה rejects his reading of the פסוק, and a ברייתא of רבי שמעון with four rules refutes him completely. The גמרא then gives a פסוק for each service the משנה says is done only at the big public altar and not on a private במה. Along the way, רב ששת teaches that bird offerings follow the same rule as a מנחה. Finally, two opposite versions of רמי בר חמא ask whether a small-במה offering brought on the big altar needs the dividing line for blood. A ברייתא about חזה ושוק is reread to fit, and the second version is shown to disagree with רבי אלעזר. The amud ends as רבי זירא begins a new question, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The split view fits the double wording of the verse
steps.stepSummary: The view that "rest" and "inheritance" are two different places (שילה and ירושלים, in either order) fits well with the פסוק's double phrase "אל המנוחה ואל הנחלה."
steps.simpleTranslation: [Granted, according to the one who says "rest" is] שילה and "inheritance" is ירושלים, or the other way around, that is why the פסוק says "to the rest AND to the inheritance."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a sentence it started just before: it shows that the view treating the two words as two different places matches how the פסוק is written. This sets up a challenge against the other two views.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק repeats the word "אֶל" ("to") before each word. That sounds like two separate places, which is exactly what this view says. The other views will now be tested against this same wording.

keyTerms.meaning: Rest; one of the two names in the פסוק
Inheritance; the second name in the פסוק
Or also the reverse
That is why it is written

phrases.english: is Shiloh, and "inheritance" is Jerusalem,
phrases.notes: This finishes a sentence from right before: "Granted, according to the one who says 'rest' is..."

phrases.english: or also the reverse —
that is why it is written:
"To the rest and to the inheritance."
phrases.notes: דברים 12:9

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the בשלמא statement begun just before this text, supporting the split view.
steps.raayaObject: The view that מנוחה and נחלה are two different places
steps.raayaSupportSource: The double "אֶל" in דברים 12:9: "אֶל הַמְּנוּחָה וְאֶל הַנַּחֲלָה"

steps.title: Challenge to the views that both words mean one place
steps.stepSummary: If both words mean שילה, or both mean ירושלים, the פסוק should simply have said "מנוחה נחלה" without the extra "to."
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to the one who says both are שילה, or both are ירושלים, the פסוק should have said "rest-inheritance" as one phrase!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the two views that make both words refer to a single place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If both words describe one place, there is no reason to say "to" twice. The repeated "אֶל" suggests two destinations, and that clashes with these views.

keyTerms.meaning: This and that; both words
It should have said

phrases.english: But according to the one who says
this and that are Shiloh,
or this and that are Jerusalem —
it should have said "rest-inheritance"!
phrases.notes: He means as one joined phrase, without repeating "to," since it is only one place.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts with step 1: what fits the split view does not fit the single-place views.
steps.kashyaTarget: The views that both מנוחה and נחלה mean שילה, or both mean ירושלים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The double "אֶל" implies two places, so a single-place reading leaves the extra word unexplained.

steps.title: The difficulty stands unanswered
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא admits it has no answer to the challenge from the wording of the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is difficult.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא concedes that the question from step 2 has no answer here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying "קשיא" leaves the question open. It does not throw out the single-place views, and the גמרא keeps discussing them right afterward. It only admits that the wording of the פסוק is hard for them.

keyTerms.meaning: It is difficult; a question left without an answer

steps.confusionAlert: "קשיא" here does not mean the opinion is rejected. It is a weakness the גמרא leaves standing, and the next steps go on to explain these same views.

phrases.english: It is difficult.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the challenge of step 2 without an answer.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The double wording of the פסוק stays a difficulty for the single-place views.

steps.title: Why שילה can be called both rest and inheritance
steps.stepSummary: For the view that both words mean שילה, "rest" fits because Israel rested from conquering the land then, and "inheritance" fits because יהושע divided the land there.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, according to the one who says both are שילה: "rest" because they rested from the conquest, and "inheritance" because they divided the portions of land there, as it is written: "And יהושע divided it for them and cast a lot for them in שילה before ה׳."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to a new question: how can one place have both names? It starts with the view that both mean שילה and explains each name easily.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The name "rest" fits the period of שילה, when the wars of conquest were over. The name "inheritance" fits because the tribes received their portions there, and a פסוק in יהושע proves it.

keyTerms.meaning: Granted; this view works fine
The conquest of the land
Tribal portions of land
A lot drawn to divide the land

phrases.english: Granted, according to the one who says
this and that are Shiloh;
"rest" — because they rested from the conquest,
"inheritance" — because they divided the portions there,
phrases.notes: Some versions don't have the word in round brackets.

phrases.english: as it is written: "And Joshua divided for them

phrases.aramaic: וַיַּפֵּל לָהֶם גּוֹרָל בְּשִׁילֹה עַל פִּי ה׳״.
phrases.english: and cast a lot for them in Shiloh before the Lord."
phrases.notes: יהושע 18:10

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר זוֹ וָזוֹ שִׁילֹה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the wording problem to explaining how one place can carry both names.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שילה is "rest" because the conquest had ended, and "inheritance" because the land was divided there.

steps.title: For ירושלים, inheritance fits, but what rest?
steps.stepSummary: For the view that both words mean ירושלים, "inheritance" fits because it is an eternal inheritance. But what "rest" belongs to ירושלים?
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to the one who says both are ירושלים: granted, "inheritance" means an eternal inheritance. But "rest": what rest is that?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now tests the view that both words mean ירושלים. One name fits easily, so it asks about the other. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ירושלים is called "inheritance" because it is permanent forever. The rest from conquest belongs to the earlier period of שילה, so the גמרא needs a different meaning of "rest" for ירושלים.

keyTerms.meaning: An eternal inheritance
What?

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר זוֹ וָזוֹ יְרוּשָׁלַיִם;
phrases.english: But according to the one who says this and that are Jerusalem;
granted, "inheritance" — an eternal inheritance.
But "rest" — what rest?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר זוֹ וָזוֹ יְרוּשָׁלַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the same name-by-name test from step 4 to the ירושלים view.

steps.title: The rest of the ארון
steps.stepSummary: "Rest" refers to the ארון finally coming to rest in ירושלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The rest of the ארון, as it is written: "And it was when the ארון rested."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: ירושלים is called "rest" because the ארון stopped traveling and settled there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ארון had moved from place to place for a long time. In the בית המקדש it found its permanent home, so ירושלים is its "resting place."

keyTerms.meaning: The Holy Ark
The resting of the Ark

steps.whatToRemember: Each place earns both names: שילה is "rest" because the conquest ended and "inheritance" because the land was divided there. ירושלים is "inheritance" because it is eternal and "rest" because the ארון rested there.

phrases.english: The rest of the Ark,
as it is written: "And it was when the Ark rested."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: מנוחה means the resting of the ארון in ירושלים.

steps.title: Private altars during the שילה period: support from מנוח
steps.stepSummary: Under the view that both words mean ירושלים, private altars (במות) were still allowed during the time of שילה. מנוח's offering on a rock fits this view.
steps.simpleTranslation: Granted, according to the one who says both are ירושלים, private altars were permitted in the time of שילה. That is why it is written: "And מנוח took the young goat and the מנחה and offered them on the rock to ה׳."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that one view fits a story in תנ״ך. This also sets up the next move: what will the other view do with this story?
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the "rest" that ends private altars is only ירושלים, then during שילה private altars were still allowed. מנוח lived in the שילה period and offered on a rock instead of at the משכן, which fits this view well. The opening word "בשלמא" hints that the other view will have trouble with this.

keyTerms.meaning: Private altars
Were permitted
Father of שמשון, who brought an offering
Rock

steps.whyThisMatters: This story becomes a test case for the opinions. The view that both words mean ירושלים explains it easily, so the view that makes שילה the "rest" will need to explain it.

phrases.english: Granted, according to the one who says
this and that are Jerusalem,
but in Shiloh private altars were permitted —
phrases.notes: Some versions have the word in round brackets; the word in square brackets is the corrected wording. Both mean "permitted."

phrases.english: that is why it is written:

phrases.aramaic: ״וַיִּקַּח מָנוֹחַ אֶת גְּדִי הָעִזִּים וְאֶת הַמִּנְחָה
phrases.english: "And Manoah took the young goat and the meal offering
and offered them on the rock to the Lord."
phrases.notes: שופטים 13:19. He brought it on a rock, a private altar, not at the משכן.

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר זוֹ וָזוֹ יְרוּשָׁלַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from explaining the names to the practical result, whether private altars were allowed during שילה, and tests it against a פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: The view that both words mean ירושלים, so במות were allowed during שילה
steps.raayaSupportSource: שופטים 13:19: מנוח offered on a rock during the שילה period

steps.title: How does the Shiloh view explain מנוח's offering?
steps.stepSummary: Under the view that both words mean שילה, במות were forbidden then. So how could מנוח offer a sacrifice on a rock?
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to the one who says both words mean שילה, and private altars were forbidden at that time, what about the פסוק 'And מנוח took'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the other view and challenges it. If במות were forbidden during שילה, מנוח should not have brought an offering outside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 7, מנוח's offering fit the ירושלים view, since במות were still allowed under that view. The שילה view holds that במות were already forbidden in the time of שילה. So מנוח's offering looks like a forbidden act, and that view needs an explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: Were forbidden

phrases.english: But according to the one who says
this and that are Shiloh,
and private altars were forbidden –
what is "And Manoah took"?
phrases.notes: שופטים 13:19

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר זוֹ וָזוֹ שִׁילֹה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Step 7 fit מנוח with the ירושלים view; now the same case is used against the שילה view.
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that both words mean שילה and במות were forbidden then
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: מנוח sacrificed outside during the שילה era, which this view says was forbidden.

steps.title: מנוח's offering was a one-time special ruling
steps.stepSummary: מנוח's offering was a הוראת שעה, a special permission for that moment only.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was a temporary ruling for that moment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that מנוח's offering was allowed only as a one-time exception.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The general rule under the שילה view stays the same: במות were forbidden. מנוח's case was a special instruction for that time, so it does not prove that במות were allowed.

keyTerms.meaning: A temporary ruling given for a special moment, not a lasting rule

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how the גמרא handles a story that seems to break a rule: it treats the story as an exception, not as a change in the law.

phrases.english: It was a provisional ruling for that moment.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 8.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: מנוח's offering shows that במות were allowed in the שילה era.
steps.terutzMaskana: במות were forbidden; מנוח's offering was a special exception for that moment.

steps.title: Another version: רבי ישמעאל's school agrees both words mean ירושלים
steps.stepSummary: In another version, דבי רבי ישמעאל taught like רבי שמעון בן יוחי, that both words mean ירושלים. The memory sign is 'the man pulled the men.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught in line with רבי שמעון בן יוחי, who says both words mean ירושלים. Your memory sign: the man pulled the men.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different version of the debate. In this version, רבי ישמעאל's school holds the same view as רבי שמעון בן יוחי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before, the two sides were רבי ישמעאל's school (שילה) and רבי שמעון בן יוחי (ירושלים). Now the גמרא reports that the school also held ירושלים. The memory sign means that one man, רבי שמעון בן יוחי, 'pulled' the group over to his opinion.

keyTerms.meaning: Your memory sign (a hint to help you remember)
The man (pulled) the men

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new argument. It is just another report of who held which view.

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught
in accordance with Rabbi Shimon ben Yoḥai,
who says: This and that are Jerusalem.
And your mnemonic:
The man pulled the men.
phrases.notes: Some versions say משכי; מַשְׁכִינְהוּ in square brackets is the corrected wording. The one man won the group over to his view.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא דְּבֵי רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל כְּרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives another version of who held each view in the debate just finished.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In this version, רבי ישמעאל's school also held that both 'rest' and 'inheritance' mean ירושלים.

steps.title: רב כהנא: the משנה's exemption from כרת covers only slaughter
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says no כרת for offerings consecrated when במות were allowed and brought outside after they became forbidden. רב כהנא limits this to שחיטה; for העלאה there is כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said 'All offerings...' רב כהנא said: they taught this only about slaughtering. But for offering up on the altar, he is also liable to כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and brings רב כהנא's limit on its rule. The no-כרת rule covers only slaughtering outside, not offering up outside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה seemed to say there is never כרת in this case. רב כהנא narrows it to שחיטה. If the person offers the animal up on an outside altar (העלאה), the regular כרת still applies.

keyTerms.meaning: They taught this only in the case of
Slaughtering the animal
Offering up (burning the offering on the altar)
Spiritual cutting off, a severe Heavenly punishment

steps.whatToRemember: The no-כרת rule in the משנה is only for slaughtering outside. Offering up outside still brings כרת.

phrases.english: "All offerings," etc.
phrases.notes: This quotes the opening words of the משנה, about offerings consecrated when במות were allowed and brought outside later.

phrases.english: Rav Kahana says:
They taught this only with regard to slaughter,
but with regard to offering up –
he is also liable to karet.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא בִּשְׁחִיטָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the שילה / ירושלים debate and returns to the next line of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For offerings consecrated when במות were allowed, slaughtering them outside later brings no כרת, but offering them up outside does.

steps.title: The פסוק behind רב כהנא's rule
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why, and answers from 'וַאֲלֵהֶם תֹּאמַר,' read as 'about the nearby passage you shall say.'
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? Because the פסוק says 'And to them you shall say,' meaning: about the passage right next to it you shall say this.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of רב כהנא's rule and brings a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אֲלֵהֶם ('to them') is read like עֲלֵיהֶם ('about them'). This connects the כרת for offering up outside to the passage right before it, which talks about those same offerings. So even where slaughtering outside brings no כרת, offering them up outside does.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
'And to them you shall say' (ויקרא 17:8)
Things placed right next to each other (nearby passages)

phrases.english: What is the reason?
Because the verse states: "And to them you shall say" –
phrases.notes: ויקרא 17:8

phrases.english: about the adjacent ones you shall say.
phrases.notes: אֲלֵהֶם sounds like עֲלֵיהֶם, 'about them,' so the פסוק points back to the passage right before it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for רב כהנא's rule in step 11.
steps.raayaObject: רב כהנא's rule that offering up outside brings כרת
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא 17:8, 'וַאֲלֵהֶם תֹּאמַר,' read as 'about the adjacent passage'

steps.title: רבה rejects the reading of the verse
steps.stepSummary: רבה argues that the פסוק says 'to them,' not 'about them,' so it cannot point to the nearby passage the way רב כהנא needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה objects: Does the פסוק say 'and about them you shall say'? It is written אֲלֵהֶם and read אֲלֵיהֶם, and both mean 'to them'!
steps.whatsHappening: רבה attacks the proof from the פסוק that was brought for רב כהנא in the previous step. He says the word simply does not mean 'about.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof depended on reading 'וַאֲלֵהֶם' as if it said 'וַעֲלֵיהֶם', meaning 'about them,' which pointed to the nearby passage. רבה points out that the way it is written and the way it is read both mean 'to them.' So the פסוק just tells משה whom to speak to. With that reading gone, רב כהנא's split between שחיטה and העלאה loses its source.

keyTerms.meaning: He objects to it; he attacks a statement or proof
It is written (how the word is spelled in the תורה)
We read it (how the word is pronounced)
'To them' versus 'about them'

steps.confusionAlert: The fight is not about the missing letter י. Whether you look at the spelling or the reading, the word starts with א ('to'), not ע ('about').

phrases.english: Rabba objects to this:
Is it written "and about them you shall say"?!
phrases.notes: He is quoting ויקרא 17:8, the פסוק used in the last step.

phrases.english: "To them" is written,
and we read it as "to them"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the verse-based proof given for רב כהנא in step 12.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The source from the פסוק for רב כהנא's split between שחיטה and העלאה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The word means 'to them,' not 'about them,' so it cannot point to the nearby passage.

steps.title: A ברייתא of רבי שמעון: the first two rules
steps.stepSummary: A second attack on רב כהנא. רבי שמעון's ברייתא says that an offering consecrated while במות were allowed and then slaughtered and offered up after they were forbidden has no כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: Furthermore, a ברייתא teaches that רבי שמעון gave four rules about offerings. First: if they were consecrated, slaughtered and offered up outside, all while במות were forbidden, there is a positive command, a prohibition, and כרת. Second: if they were consecrated while במות were allowed, then slaughtered and offered up while במות were forbidden, there is a positive command and a prohibition, but no כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a second, stronger challenge to רב כהנא from a ברייתא. This step brings the first two of רבי שמעון's four rules.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second rule is the key one. It covers exactly רב כהנא's case, and it says 'slaughtered AND offered up' with no כרת. That means העלאה also has no כרת, which goes against רב כהנא, who said העלאה does carry כרת.

keyTerms.meaning: General rules
A time when private altars were forbidden / a time when they were allowed
A positive command and a prohibition

phrases.english: And furthermore, it is taught in a ברייתא:

phrases.aramaic: אַרְבָּעָה כְּלָלוֹת הָיָה רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר בְּקָדָשִׁים:
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon would say four rules about sacrificial animals:
If he consecrated them when private altars were forbidden,
and slaughtered and offered them up
outside, when private altars were forbidden,
these fall under a positive command and a prohibition,
and they carry the punishment of כרת.
If he consecrated them when private altars were allowed,
and slaughtered and offered them up when private altars were forbidden,
these fall under a positive command and a prohibition,
but they do not carry כרת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second challenge to רב כהנא, this time from a ברייתא, on top of רבה's objection to the reading.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב כהנא's ruling that העלאה carries כרת in this case.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא puts 'slaughtered and offered up' together in the same case and says there is no כרת, so it makes no split between שחיטה and העלאה.

steps.title: The ברייתא continues: the last two rules
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון's third and fourth rules finish the full chart of possible cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: Third: if consecrated while במות were forbidden, then slaughtered and offered up outside while they were allowed, there is a positive command but no prohibition. Fourth: if consecrated and also slaughtered and offered up while במות were allowed, he is completely exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא finishes its list of four rules. Every combination of 'consecrated when' and 'brought when' is now covered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The four rules form a simple chart. When the offering is brought out decides whether there is a prohibition. כרת comes only when both the consecration and the bringing happened while במות were forbidden. In none of the rules does the ברייתא treat slaughtering differently from offering up.

keyTerms.meaning: Exempt from everything
He consecrated them (set them aside as offerings)

steps.whatToRemember: The four rules: forbidden then forbidden = עשה + לא תעשה + כרת. Allowed then forbidden = עשה + לא תעשה, no כרת. Forbidden then allowed = עשה only. Allowed then allowed = exempt.

phrases.english: If he consecrated them when private altars were forbidden,

phrases.aramaic: וְשָׁחַט וְהֶעֱלָה בַּחוּץ בִּשְׁעַת הֶיתֵּר הַבָּמוֹת –
phrases.english: and slaughtered and offered them up outside when private altars were allowed,
these fall under a positive command,
but they do not fall under a prohibition.
If he consecrated them when private altars were allowed,
and slaughtered and offered them up when private altars were allowed,
he is exempt from everything.

steps.triggerLanguage: הִקְדִּישָׁן בִּשְׁעַת אִיסּוּר הַבָּמוֹת, וְשָׁחַט וְהֶעֱלָה בַּחוּץ בִּשְׁעַת הֶיתֵּר הַבָּמוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא, finishing the four rules.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב כהנא's split between שחיטה and העלאה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Even the full set of rules never separates slaughtering from offering up, so the ברייתא clearly treats them alike.

steps.title: רב כהנא is refuted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the ברייתא is a full refutation of רב כהנא.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is a refutation of רב כהנא! Indeed, it is a refutation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא announces the challenge and then confirms it. רב כהנא's view does not stand.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying תְּיוּבְתָּא twice means the question has no answer. The הלכה follows the ברייתא: when an offering was consecrated while במות were allowed, there is no כרת for either שחיטה or העלאה done after they became forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: A refutation; a final, unanswered challenge

steps.whatToRemember: רב כהנא's split between שחיטה and העלאה is rejected. If the offering was consecrated while במות were allowed, there is no כרת for either act.
steps.whyThisMatters: A double תְּיוּבְתָּא closes the question for good. רב כהנא's ruling is no longer followed.

phrases.english: This is a refutation of Rav Kahana!
It is a refutation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the challenge from the ברייתא with a final ruling against רב כהנא.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב כהנא is refuted. There is no כרת for either שחיטה or העלאה when the offering was consecrated while במות were allowed.

steps.title: Sources for leaning hands and slaughtering in the north
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's list of services done only in the משכן and gives פסוקים for סמיכה and שחיטת צפון. Both פסוקים say 'לפני ה׳'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And these are the consecrated items, etc.' Where do we learn that סמיכה is only in the משכן? The פסוק says 'before ה׳. And he shall lean.' Where do we learn שחיטת צפון? The פסוק says 'northward before ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new section. It goes back to the משנה's list and begins showing where each service comes from in the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה listed services that happen at the big public מזבח but not on a private במה. For סמיכה and שחיטת צפון, the פסוקים use the words 'לפני ה׳', 'before ה׳'. That ties these services to the place of the אוהל מועד, so they are not done on a private במה.

keyTerms.meaning: Leaning one's hands on the head of the animal before it is offered
Slaughtering the offering on the north side of the מזבח
'Before ה׳', the phrase that links these services to the משכן
An altar outside the משכן or מקדש. It can be a big public one or a small private one

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the earlier argument about רב כהנא. The גמרא has moved on and is now explaining a new line of the משנה.

phrases.english: "And these are the consecrated items, etc."
phrases.notes: The גמרא is quoting the משנה's list of things done only at the big public מזבח, not at a private במה.

phrases.english: Leaning hands: as it is written:
"before ה׳. And he shall lean."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 1:3–4

phrases.english: Slaughtering in the north: as it is written:
"northward before ה׳."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 1:11

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the refutation of רב כהנא, the גמרא returns to the משנה and starts finding sources for its list.
steps.raayaObject: That סמיכה and שחיטת צפון belong only at the משכן and not on a private במה
steps.raayaSupportSource: ויקרא 1:3–4 and ויקרא 1:11, both of which say 'לפני ה׳'

steps.title: Sources for putting blood all around, waving, and bringing to the altar
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives פסוקים for the rest of the list: מתנות סביב, תנופה, and הגשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: מתנות סביב comes from the פסוק 'And he shall sprinkle it on the מזבח all around.' תנופה comes from 'And the כהן shall wave it before ה׳.' הגשה comes from 'And he shall bring it to the מזבח.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the list from the משנה. It gives a source in the תורה for each of the three remaining services.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each פסוק points to the one known מזבח or to 'לפני ה׳'. That shows these services belong to the משכן. תנופה again uses 'לפני ה׳'. מתנות סביב and הגשה speak about 'the מזבח', meaning the specific מזבח of the משכן.

keyTerms.meaning: Putting the blood on all sides of the מזבח
Waving parts of certain offerings back and forth
Bringing a מנחה to the corner of the מזבח before the handful is taken
'The מזבח', meaning the specific מזבח of the משכן

steps.whatToRemember: Every service on the משנה's list has a פסוק that ties it to the משכן, either through 'לפני ה׳' or through 'the מזבח'. That is why none of them is done on a private במה.

phrases.english: Placing the blood all around: as it is written:
"And he shall sprinkle it on the altar all around."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 1:5. The פסוק says סָבִיב only once, so the corrected wording leaves out the second one in round brackets.

phrases.english: Waving: as it is written:
"And the priest shall wave it before ה׳."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 14:12

phrases.english: Bringing near: as it is written:
"And he shall bring it to the altar."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 2:8

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same list of sources begun in step 17.
steps.raayaObject: That מתנות סביב, תנופה, and הגשה belong only at the משכן

steps.title: Bird offerings follow the same rule as a מנחה on a במה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי יהודה's view that there is no מנחה on a במה. רב ששת then rules that עופות go together with מנחה: whoever allows a מנחה on a במה allows birds, and whoever forbids one forbids the other.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה says: there is no מנחה on a במה. רב ששת said: according to the one who says a מנחה may be brought on a במה, birds may also be brought on a במה. According to the one who says no מנחה may be brought on a במה, birds may not be brought on a במה either.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה, רבי יהודה's view about מנחה on a במה. רב ששת then adds a rule that connects bird offerings to the same argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only argues about מנחה. רב ששת teaches that the argument also covers עופות, so both sides keep birds and מנחה together. He does not create a new opinion. He extends each existing opinion to a second kind of offering.

keyTerms.meaning: A flour offering
Bird offerings, such as doves and pigeons
'According to the one who says', which means following that opinion

steps.whyThisMatters: רב ששת's rule means the משנה's argument about מנחה decides the law for birds too. Whatever we hold for one, we hold for the other.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
There is no meal offering on a במה.
Rav Sheshet said:
According to the one who says there is a meal offering on a במה,
there are bird offerings on a במה.
According to the one who says there is no meal offering on a במה,
there are no bird offerings on a במה.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: לְדִבְרֵי הָאוֹמֵר יֵשׁ מִנְחָה בְּבָמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finishing the sources for the list, the גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה, רבי יהודה's view on מנחה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Bird offerings follow מנחה: if a מנחה is allowed on a במה, so are birds; if not, birds are not allowed either.

steps.title: Only animal offerings on a במה, not meal offerings or birds
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives the source for the view that no מנחה and no bird offering was brought on a במה: the פסוק calls those offerings 'זבחים'.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'זבחים' (slaughtered animal offerings). That means animals, not meal offerings. It also means animals, not birds.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the view from the last step that there is no מנחה and no bird offering on a במה. It reads the word 'זבחים' as limiting the offerings to animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה describes the offerings brought outside the משכן as 'זבחים', which means slaughtered animals. A מנחה is flour, not a slaughtered animal, so it is left out. Birds are left out as well. This is why רב ששת said that מנחה and birds always go together.

keyTerms.meaning: Slaughtered animal offerings
Meal offerings, made of flour

steps.confusionAlert: Birds are also slaughtered, yet the word 'זבחים' is still read as leaving them out. In this reading, 'זבחים' means animal offerings only.

phrases.english: "Slaughtered offerings": and not meal offerings,
phrases.notes: This comes from the פסוק about offerings brought outside: 'וזבחו זבחי שלמים' (ויקרא 17:5).

phrases.english: "Slaughtered offerings": and not birds.

steps.triggerLanguage: זְבָחִים וְלֹא מְנָחוֹת זְבָחִים וְלֹא עוֹפוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק behind רבי יהודה's view, and behind רב ששת's rule that birds go together with מנחה
steps.raayaObject: No מנחה and no bird offering on a במה
steps.raayaSupportSource: The word 'זבחים' in the פסוק about offerings outside the משכן (ויקרא 17:5)

steps.title: Sources for needing a כהן, priestly clothing, and service vessels
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the משנה's list of things needed only in the משכן. It gives פסוקים for a כהן, בגדי שרת, and כלי שרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: A כהן is needed, because it says 'and the כהן shall sprinkle'. Priestly clothing is needed, because it says 'to serve in the holy place'. Service vessels are needed, because it says 'with which they serve in the holy place'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues giving a פסוק for each item on the משנה's list. Here it covers the people and the equipment: a כהן, his special clothing, and the holy vessels.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each of these פסוקים connects the service to the holy place of the משכן. So these requirements apply there, and not on a private במה. This continues the same pattern as steps 17 and 18.

keyTerms.meaning: A priest, a descendant of אהרן
The special clothing a כהן wears for the service
The holy vessels used in the service
In the holy place

phrases.english: And a priest: as it is written:
"And the priest shall sprinkle."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 17:6

phrases.english: Service garments: "to serve in the holy place."
phrases.notes: שמות 28:43

phrases.english: And service vessels:
"with which they serve in the holy place."
phrases.notes: במדבר 4:12

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the list from steps 17-18 after the side point about מנחה and birds
steps.raayaObject: A כהן, בגדי שרת, and כלי שרת are needed only in the משכן

steps.title: Sources for ריח ניחוח, the dividing line for blood, and washing hands
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes the list. It gives פסוקים for ריח ניחוח, the dividing line on the מזבח for the blood, and washing hands.
steps.simpleTranslation: For a pleasing smell, it says 'a pleasing smell to ה׳'. For the dividing line for blood, it says 'and the net shall reach halfway up the מזבח'. For washing hands, it says 'and when they come near to the מזבח, they shall wash'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the last three פסוקים, which complete the משנה's list of things needed only in the משכן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These פסוקים speak about 'the מזבח' of the משכן, with its net halfway up and the washing before coming near it. So these rules belong to the משכן's מזבח and not to a private במה. With this, every item on the list has its own source.

keyTerms.meaning: A pleasing smell to ה׳
A dividing line
The net or grating around the מזבח
Washing the hands (and feet) before doing the service

steps.whatToRemember: Every item on the משנה's list of things needed only in the משכן (and not on a במה) has its own פסוק. Most of these פסוקים mention the holy place or the מזבח of the משכן.

phrases.english: For a pleasing aroma: as it is written:
phrases.notes: This means limbs that were already roasted away from the מזבח may not then be put on it.

phrases.english: "for a pleasing aroma to the Lord."
A partition for the blood: as it is written:
phrases.notes: This is the red line around the middle of the מזבח. Some blood went above it and some went below it.

phrases.english: "And the net shall reach halfway up the altar."
phrases.notes: שמות 27:5

phrases.english: Washing of hands: as it is written:
"And when they come near to the altar, they shall wash."
phrases.notes: שמות 40:32

steps.triggerLanguage: לְרֵיחַ נִיחוֹחַ דִּכְתִיב לְרֵיחַ נִיחֹחַ לַה׳
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues and finishes the list of פסוקים begun in step 21
steps.raayaObject: ריח ניחוח, the dividing line for blood, and washing hands are needed only in the משכן

steps.title: First version: where the animal is offered decides
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר חמא says the משנה's rule of no חיצוי applies only to an animal set aside for a small בָּמָה and also brought on a small בָּמָה. If it was set aside for a small בָּמָה but brought on the big בָּמָה, it does get a חיצוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר חמא said: The משנה only taught that there is no dividing line when the offering was meant for a small altar and was brought on a small altar. But if it was meant for a small altar and was brought on the big altar, there is a dividing line.
steps.whatsHappening: רמי בר חמא limits the משנה's rule. He says a קרבן meant for a private altar still needs the dividing line if it is actually brought on the big public altar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two factors: what the animal was set aside for, and where it is actually offered. In this version, the place of offering decides. The big altar's rules apply to whatever is brought on it.

keyTerms.meaning: A small private altar, which was allowed in certain periods
The big public altar, at the משכן
Offerings set aside for a certain kind of altar
The dividing line on the מזבח that separates upper and lower blood placements
They only taught this about... (a phrase that limits a rule)

phrases.english: Rami bar Ḥama said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא בְּקׇדְשֵׁי בָּמָה קְטַנָּה,
phrases.english: They taught it only about offerings set aside for a small altar,
phrases.notes: "It" is the משנה's rule that a small altar has no dividing line for the blood.

phrases.english: which were offered on a small altar;
but offerings set aside for a small altar
that were offered on the big altar –
there is a dividing line.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the חיצוי item from the list in Step 22 and asks how it applies to a mixed case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The place of offering decides, so a small-בָּמָה offering brought on the big בָּמָה needs a חיצוי.

steps.title: רבה challenges from a ברייתא about חזה ושוק
steps.stepSummary: רבה quotes a ברייתא: חזה ושוק and תרומת לחמי תודה apply to offerings of the big בָּמָה but not to offerings of the small בָּמָה. This sounds like the designation decides, not the place.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבה objected: The breast and thigh, and the תרומה of the תודה loaves, apply to offerings of the big altar and do not apply to offerings of a small altar.
steps.whatsHappening: רבה brings a ברייתא that seems to go against רמי בר חמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says "offerings of a small altar" have no חזה ושוק. That sounds like an animal set aside for a small altar keeps the small-altar rules even if it is brought on the big altar. That goes against what רמי בר חמא just said.

keyTerms.meaning: The breast and thigh of a שלמים, which are waved and given to the כהן
The portion of the תודה loaves given to the כהן
Apply, are in effect

phrases.english: Rabba raised an objection:
The breast and thigh, and the teruma of the thanks-offering loaves –
apply to offerings of the big altar,
and do not apply to offerings of a small altar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks Step 23 with a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רמי בר חמא's claim that the place of offering decides
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא ties the rules to "offerings of" each altar, which suggests the designation decides even when the animal is brought on the big altar.

steps.title: Reread the ברייתא as talking about the place
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the ברייתא should be read as "applies at the big בָּמָה, does not apply at the small בָּמָה." Now it is about the place, which fits רמי בר חמא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say instead: they apply at the big altar, and they do not apply at a small altar.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רמי בר חמא by changing how the ברייתא is worded.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once "offerings of" is dropped, the ברייתא only says which altar the rules apply at. A small-altar animal brought on the big altar would then get חזה ושוק, just as רמי בר חמא said it gets a חיצוי.

keyTerms.meaning: Say instead; reread the text this way

phrases.english: Say: they apply at the big altar,
and do not apply at a small altar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבה's challenge in Step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to say the designation decides.
steps.terutzMaskana: Read correctly, the ברייתא speaks about the place of offering, so it fits רמי בר חמא.

steps.title: Second version: what the animal was set aside for decides
steps.stepSummary: Some report that רמי בר חמא said the opposite: חיצוי applies only to big-בָּמָה offerings brought on the big בָּמָה. A small-בָּמָה offering gets no חיצוי even if it is brought on the big בָּמָה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say רמי בר חמא said: They taught the dividing line only about offerings of the big altar that were brought on the big altar. But offerings of a small altar, even if they were brought on the big altar, have no dividing line.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second report of what רמי בר חמא said, and it gives the opposite ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the designation decides. An animal set aside for a private altar keeps its private-altar rules even on the big altar, so there is no חיצוי.

keyTerms.meaning: Even though

steps.confusionAlert: Both versions are reports of what רמי בר חמא said, and they come out opposite. In the first, the place of offering decides. In the second, what the animal was set aside for decides.

phrases.aramaic: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי, אָמַר רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא:
phrases.english: Some say: Rami bar Ḥama said:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא בְּקׇדְשֵׁי בָּמָה גְּדוֹלָה,
phrases.english: They taught it only about offerings of the big altar,
phrases.notes: Here "it" is the rule that there is a dividing line.

phrases.english: which were offered on the big altar;
but offerings of a small altar –

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּקָרְבִינְהוּ בְּבָמָה גְּדוֹלָה,
phrases.english: even though they were offered on the big altar,
there is no dividing line.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי, אָמַר רָמֵי בַּר חָמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second, opposite report of the teaching in Step 23.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The designation decides, so a small-בָּמָה offering brought on the big בָּמָה has no חיצוי.

steps.title: The same ברייתא seems to support the second version
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the ברייתא about חזה ושוק supports the second version, since it says these rules do not apply to "offerings of a small בָּמָה."
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say this supports him: The breast and thigh, and the תרומה of the תודה loaves, apply to offerings of the big altar and do not apply to offerings of a small altar.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers the ברייתא from Step 24 as a possible proof for the second version of רמי בר חמא. The word "shall we say" tells us the גמרא is testing this proof and may push it away next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Read plainly, "offerings of a small altar" means what the animal was set aside for. That fits the second version well: a small-altar animal keeps small-altar rules even on the big altar. The same ברייתא that was a problem for the first version now looks like support for the second.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say this supports him? (often followed by a rejection)

steps.whyThisMatters: The same ברייתא is read two ways: by place for the first version, and by designation for the second. This shows how one wording choice can decide the question.

phrases.english: Shall we say this supports him:
phrases.notes: "Him" is רמי בר חמא in the second version.

phrases.english: The breast and thigh, and the teruma of the thanks-offering loaves –
apply to offerings of the big altar,
and do not apply to offerings of a small altar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a proof for the second version given in Step 26.
steps.raayaObject: The second version: designation decides, so there is no חיצוי
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא about חזה ושוק and תרומת לחמי תודה, read as "offerings of" each altar

steps.title: The proof is pushed off: read the ברייתא as being about the place
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof for the second version of רמי בר חמא. It rereads the ברייתא to mean: these rules apply at the big בָּמָה and do not apply at the small בָּמָה.
steps.simpleTranslation: I can say the ברייתא means: these rules apply at the big בָּמָה, and they do not apply at the small בָּמָה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes away the proof from step 27. It says the ברייתא can be read as being about where the offering is brought, not what it was set aside for.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 27 read "offerings of a small בָּמָה" as being about what the animal was set aside for. Under that reading, a small-בָּמָה animal never gets these rules. The גמרא answers that the ברייתא can just as well mean "at a small בָּמָה." On that reading, a small-בָּמָה animal brought to the big בָּמָה does get them, so the ברייתא no longer proves the second version.
steps.confusionAlert: This is the same rereading the גמרא used in step 25. There it answered a challenge. Here it blocks a proof.

phrases.english: Say: they apply at the big בָּמָה,
phrases.notes: "They" means the rules of חזה ושוק and תרומת לחמי תודה from the ברייתא in step 24.

phrases.english: and they do not apply at the small בָּמָה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof offered in step 27 by rereading the ברייתא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the ברייתא. It does not disprove the second version of רמי בר חמא.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The ברייתא can be read as being about the place of offering, not the designation, so it gives no support either way.

steps.title: The second version disagrees with רבי אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the second version of רמי בר חמא disagrees with רבי אלעזר. רבי אלעזר says a small-בָּמָה עולה brought inside is taken in by the walls for every matter.
steps.simpleTranslation: This disagrees with רבי אלעזר, who said: a עולה of a private בָּמָה that someone brought inside is taken in by the walls for every matter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notes that the second version of רמי בר חמא clashes with a ruling of רבי אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אלעזר says that once a small-בָּמָה offering enters the big בָּמָה's area, the walls make it a full big-בָּמָה offering in every way. That means it would get all big-בָּמָה rules, including חיצוי. The second version said a small-בָּמָה animal gets no חיצוי even when brought to the big בָּמָה, so the two disagree.

keyTerms.meaning: and it disagrees
a private altar (the same as a small בָּמָה)
they took it in / absorbed it
the walls/partitions (of the big בָּמָה's area)

steps.whyThisMatters: רבי אלעזר's idea, that entering the walls changes an offering's status completely, is the background for רבי זירא's question that follows.

phrases.english: And this disagrees with רבי אלעזר,
phrases.notes: "This" is the second version of רמי בר חמא's statement from step 26.

phrases.english: for רבי אלעזר said:
A burnt offering of a private altar
that one brought inside –
phrases.notes: "Inside" means into the area of the big, public בָּמָה.

phrases.english: the walls took it in for every matter.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Having blocked the proof, the גמרא notes that the second version conflicts with רבי אלעזר's ruling.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A private-בָּמָה עולה brought into the big בָּמָה's area becomes a full big-בָּמָה offering in every way.

steps.title: רבי זירא begins a question about a private-בָּמָה עולה
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא opens a question about a עולה of a private בָּמָה. The question itself continues past this point.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא asked: a עולה of a private בָּמָה,
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא starts a new question about a private-בָּמָה עולה. This line is only the opening, setting up the full question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question builds on רבי אלעזר's idea that bringing such an offering inside changes its status. The exact case רבי זירא asks about is not stated yet; it follows in the next part of the text.

keyTerms.meaning: he asked (raised a question he was unsure about)
a burnt offering, burned completely on the altar

phrases.english: רבי זירא asked:
A burnt offering of a private altar,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question that grows out of רבי אלעזר's ruling about a private-בָּמָה עולה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How the law treats a private-בָּמָה עולה in a case still to be stated (the question continues in the next part of the text).
